thread:
maya: FYI — AcmeHealth (acct acme-42) escalated: truncated SSE payload after reconnect via their corporate proxy. final JSON chunk missing and no finish_reason.
customer_acme: We get a partial JSON, parser fails. Happens on reconnect, not on first stream.
maya: Repro notes from them: they open EventSource to /v1/streams with Authorization header through proxy, then simulate a network drop, then reconnect with Resume header. On reconnect the stream returns bytes that end mid-JSON and then the connection is closed.
customer_acme: Example: stream ends like `... \"content\": \"...partial text\"` then EOF. No `{\"finish_reason\":...}`.
ryan: Do we have their request id / timestamps? Any raw bytes?
maya: They provided req id `req_0a3b9c` and a hexdump + pcap attached to the ticket. Also said direct calls (no proxy) don't reproduce.
maya: Their curl repro:
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Resume-From: 12345" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=rw-1"
```
olivia: Sounds like proxy may be trimming the final event or closing mid-event. Similar but not identical to another ticket I saw.
eng-runtime-bot: Logged. Hypothesis: proxy/edge is closing connection without allowing our final flush, or our resume handling miscomputes last-frame offset.
ryan: Requesting: raw bytes, exact resume header value, whether connection used HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1, and client library version.
customer_acme: They use Node EventSource polyfill v2.0 behind a corporate Fastly-ish proxy. They attached pcap and hexdump to the ticket.
maya: Also observed latency spike ~700ms before reconnect.
ryan: I repro'd internally by routing through a similar proxy and saw truncated last event when the proxy force-closed while we were writing the trailing newline.
olivia: Workaround for customer: validate JSON on client; if parse fails, resume with last-good-token or set a `start_over` flag to re-run. Not ideal but reduces immediate impact.
eng-runtime-bot: Action items created: 1) runtime team to add an explicit final sentinel write + flush before FIN, 2) emit extra logging when finish_reason would have been sent, 3) add stricter resume-token validation to avoid ambiguous resume offsets.
ryan: I'll add socket-level flush/linger handling and instrument staging. Possible root cause: our HTTP stack buffers last bytes not sent if FIN races close.
support-bot: Escalation ESCL-3421 created (Severity: High). Customer impacted in production. Next update in ~2h.
maya: Customer asked whether they're billed for truncated responses — they saw token usage charged.
olivia: Billing note: token charges reflect tokens generated server-side; if compute produced final tokens but they were truncated in transit, billing may still apply. I'll loop in billing to confirm and make an exception if needed.
ryan: For my repro I need the exact timeline from the pcap and the resume header numeric offsets. @maya please attach the pcap link to ESCL-3421. Also check for any retry middleware that might strip trailing bytes.
maya: Uploaded pcap/hexdump. They also said proxy injects a `Via` header and does TLS termination.
eng-runtime-bot: Recommended temporary server mitigation: on connection close, attempt to write a final `event: done\ndata: {\"finish_reason\":\"server_close\"}\n\n` sentinel before closing socket. We'll canary that in staging.
ryan: Quick canary script to reproduce locally:
```
node repro.js --proxy fastly --drop-after 500ms
```
olivia: Looping in billing + security. @customer_acme we're investigating; ETA to update: 2h 👍 
customer_acme: Thanks for the quick response. Please let us know if you need more traces.
support-bot: ESCL-3421 update: Eng assigned (ryan), canary planned, tentative rollback/patch window 4h.
maya: Will follow up to the customer once canary confirms fix. Thanks team!
